evidence.quote: All automation features in Covidence are optional and can be turned off

ai_features.note: AI features: relevance sorting, RCT tagging and removal (EPPI-Centre classifiers), and LLM extraction and intervention suggestions. Extraction suggestions are enabled by default in a review.

evidence.quote: Covidence uses Google's Gemini models through Vertex AI.

ai_providers.note: Gemini (via Google Cloud Vertex AI) for extraction and intervention suggestions; the full-text PDF or text extracted from it is sent to the model. Screening features use classifiers developed by the EPPI-Centre; where they run is not stated.

evidence.quote: aggregating and incorporating Review Data as part of new data sets, and making those data sets available for non-commercial purposes, including the development of machine learning models.
Your unpublished data, extracted results, and proprietary comments are not used to train public-facing AI models without your explicit consent.
Google does not use customer data to train or fine-tune models under its terms and conditions for Google Cloud Services.

trains_on_content.note: The terms grant Covidence a perpetual, worldwide licence to Review Data (excluding personal information) that names the development of machine learning models as a use of aggregated data sets, with no opt-out described. Help pages and a blog say uploaded documents are not used to train AI models, unpublished data is not used for public-facing models without explicit consent, the LLM features are prompt-based with no direct training, and Google does not train on the data. The vendor does not reconcile the licence with these statements; recorded as 'yes' because the binding terms allow it.

evidence.quote: We rely on trusted large language models that don’t store or share anything from your uploaded files
Documents uploaded to the platform are not stored or shared by LLM providers and are not used to train AI models.

ai_zero_retention.note: Stated in a help article and a blog post; no contract term or provider setting (e.g. Vertex AI zero data retention) is cited.

ai_act_statement.note: No EU AI Act statement found. Read the responsible automation articles, model cards, AI FAQ and three AI blog posts; they cite Cochrane and RAISE guidance only.
